## Where it lives

The preparation-time filter is `resolveTools` in **`packages/opencode/src/session/llm/request.ts:210–216`**. It is a private helper of the request-preparation entry point `prepare` (`LLMRequestPrep.prepare`, declared at `request.ts:56`), which calls it at `request.ts:148` (`const tools = resolveTools(input)`). `prepare` is itself invoked by the LLM stream service at **`packages/opencode/src/session/llm.ts:106–113`**; the resulting `prepared.tools` is what is later handed to the model (`llm.ts:233`, `llm.ts:318`). The helper is therefore squarely in *preparation* (building the request's tool map), not in tool execution.

## The filter

```ts
// request.ts:210-216
function resolveTools(input: Pick<PrepareInput, "tools" | "agent" | "permission" | "user">) {
  const disabled = Permission.disabled(
    Object.keys(input.tools),
    Permission.merge(input.agent.permission, input.permission ?? []),
  )
  return Record.filter(input.tools, (_, k) => input.user.tools?.[k] !== false && !disabled.has(k))
}
```

Inputs: `input.tools` are the already-available tools (`PrepareInput.tools`, `request.ts:30`); `input.user` is the triggering `SessionV1.User` message (`request.ts:21`); `input.permission` is an optional request/session ruleset (`request.ts:26`).

## Permission merge order

`Permission.merge(input.agent.permission, input.permission ?? [])` (`request.ts:213`). `merge` just concatenates rulesets in order — `permission/index.ts:200–202`:

```ts
export function merge(...rulesets: PermissionV1.Ruleset[]): PermissionV1.Rule[] {
  return rulesets.flat()
}
```

So agent rules come first, request/session rules last. Because rule lookup uses `findLast` (below), the **last matching rule wins**, i.e. request/session permission overrides the agent's. (Config/user defaults were already folded into `agent.permission` upstream — e.g. `packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts:119,138,277` — but within `resolveTools` only these two rulesets are merged.)

## Message-toggle values that exclude a tool

`input.user.tools?.[k] !== false` (`request.ts:215`). Only an **explicit `false`** removes a tool. `true` and an absent entry (`undefined`, via optional chaining) both keep it. The per-message map's shape is confirmed by the (deprecated) prompt input schema `tools: Schema.optional(Schema.Record(Schema.String, Schema.Boolean))` at `prompt.ts:1505–1508`, annotated "@deprecated tools and permissions have been merged…".

## How a permission rule is chosen and disables a tool

`Permission.disabled` (`permission/index.ts:204–214`) normalizes each tool name to a permission key, then selects the rule:

```ts
const rule = ruleset.findLast((rule) => Wildcard.match(permission, rule.permission))
return rule?.pattern === "*" && rule.action === "deny"
```

Two conditions must both hold to disable: (a) the **last** matching rule by wildcard match on the permission key, and (b) that rule is a catch-all `pattern === "*"` with `action === "deny"`. A `deny` on a narrower glob (e.g. `*.ts`) does **not** hide the tool here — it remains visible and would instead be handled by runtime permission enforcement. `visibleTools` (`permission/index.ts:216–219`) applies the same `disabled` set to a tool record.

## Editing vs. MCP-resource grouping

Grouping is in `permission/index.ts:205–209`:

```ts
const edits = ["edit", "write", "apply_patch"]
const reads = ["list_mcp_resources", "list_mcp_resource_templates", "read_mcp_resource"]
const permission = edits.includes(tool) ? "edit" : reads.includes(tool) ? "read" : tool
```

- **Editing tools** `edit`, `write`, `apply_patch` → permission key `"edit"`.
- **MCP-resource-reading tools** `list_mcp_resources`, `list_mcp_resource_templates`, `read_mcp_resource` → permission key `"read"`.
- Everything else uses its own tool name as the permission key.

These same MCP tool names appear as the session tool aliases in `packages/opencode/src/session/tools.ts:28–30` (`list`, `listTemplates`, `read`).

## Boundary / related-but-separate code

Other `visibleTools` uses for MCP tools exist in `packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts:285–286` and `packages/opencode/src/tool/code-mode.ts:209–210`, and a workflow pre-approval ruleset is computed at `llm.ts:149–153`. Those are distinct from the LLM-request tool filtering asked about.

## Limitations

I verified the filter, merge, rule selection, toggle semantics, and name grouping from the cited spans. I did not read the `@opencode-ai/schema/session-v1` `User` definition (the grep for it was rejected when the tool dispatch budget was exhausted), so the `User.tools` field is inferred from the runtime check at `request.ts:215` plus the deprecated `PromptInput.tools` schema at `prompt.ts:1505`; the `Wildcard` matcher's internals were likewise not opened. No code or tests were executed.
